subject: Pin exception request: Orpheus-13B-lite deployability gap
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlas.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas AI EngOps <engops@atlas.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orpheus-13B-lite onboarding - quantization failures on Redwood

Hi Maya,

Quick note from our infra team: we attempted to onboard Orpheus-13B-lite (quantized int8) via your intake API and ran into repeated inference failures in the KV cache layer when sequences exceed ~1.6k tokens. Trace attached (orch-deploy-logs.tar.gz). We suspect the quantization path on your runtime is not compatible with the sharded KV layout Orpheus uses.

Atlas is on a tight timeline to ship a pilot with this variant next quarter. Would it be possible to request a temporary pin to Orpheus-13B (unquantized) while you validate a fix for the lite variant? We can accept a short-term SLA hit and restrict traffic to a canary.

What we need from Redwood: a compatibility check, estimated work to fix the quantized path, and a short-term pin/rollout plan if you approve.

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, Atlas AI
liam.oconnor@atlas.ai
From: maya.srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Orpheus-13B-lite onboarding - quantization failures on Redwood

Forwarding Atlas report — attaching logs they shared.

Ask: Can infra + runtime validate the root cause and give a recommendation by EOD tomorrow? Specifically:
- Short technical summary of the incompatibility (one paragraph)
- Estimated effort to make quantized path compatible (days / SRE impact)
- Proposed temporary mitigation: pin to unquantized Orpheus-13B OR a runtime flag/workaround (what we can support operationally)
- Any customer-facing risks (latency/cost/throughput) and suggested canary guardrails

Dev / Laura — can you take the lead on the compatibility check? Vivek, flagging for decision on temporary exception if needed.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: maya.srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas AI EngOps <engops@atlas.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orpheus-13B-lite onboarding - quantization failures on Redwood

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 09:12 AM Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@atlas.ai> wrote:
> Quick note from our infra team: we attempted to onboard Orpheus-13B-lite (quantized int8) via your intake API and ran into repeated inference failures in the KV cache layer when sequences exceed ~1.6k tokens. Trace attached (orch-deploy-logs.tar.gz).

Summary after initial triage:
- Root cause: a mismatch between the model's KV shard layout (Orpheus-lite expects contiguous KV segments per layer) and our quantized mmap-backed cache accessor which assumes interleaved shards for int8 kernels. This causes incorrect KV offsets for long sequences, producing NaNs and OOMs.
- Repro: deterministic locally with Atlas logs and our unit harness (see compat-check-summary.pdf).

Workaround options (pros/cons):
1) Immediate pin to Orpheus-13B (float32) for Atlas only — low effort, operationally simple, higher memory and token-cost for Atlas. Canary traffic can be limited to 5% initially.
2) Runtime shim: add an accessor compatibility layer that translates Orpheus-lite's KV layout to our int8 accessor. Estimated 3-5 engineer-days + 1 SRE day for canary and monitoring. Requires a short pause on autoscaling for the canary window.
3) Reject onboarding of Orpheus-lite until model vendor publishes a compatible quantized export — high friction.

Recommendation: approve option 1 (pin to float32 Orpheus-13B) for up to 14 calendar days while we ship the runtime shim (option 2) as a targeted fix. Short pin limits customer exposure and gives us time for a robust fix.

Attachments: compat-check-summary.pdf (2-page triage and repro steps), orch-deploy-logs.tar.gz (logs).

Next steps if approved:
- Laura: can you draft the temporary pin config (tenant-level override, canary percent, telemetry hooks) and add it to the rollout queue?
- Maya: please escalate decision to product leadership and confirm SLAs Atlas is willing to accept for the pinned variant.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: maya.srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orpheus-13B-lite onboarding - quantization failures on Redwood

Thanks for the clear analysis, Dev.

Decision: approve a targeted, timeboxed pin to Orpheus-13B (float32) for Atlas AI for up to 14 days, with the following conditions:
- Laura to own the pin config and ensure canary at 5% with automatic rollback at 3x error rate baseline.
- Dev to deliver the runtime shim as priority P0; if ETA slips beyond 10 calendar days notify leadership.
- Product to add an explicit customer-facing note about increased memory/cost during the pinned window (Maya).
- Instrumentation: full token-level telemetry and a special alert to SRE on KV errors for the pinned tenant.

Legal: no extra contract language needed for a temporary operational pin; Finance should not offer credits at this stage. If Atlas requests credits escalate to sales.

Maya — please communicate the plan to Atlas Ops and confirm the canary start date. Once Atlas agrees, Laura and Dev coordinate the rollout.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
